text.p: A five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon met on Sunday in south Lebanon to look into Israeli and Lebanese complaints over alleged breaches, security sources said.

They said the representatives of the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel began the meeting early on Sunday in the coastal town of Naqoura in south Lebanon, to consider a complaint by Beirut that Israel shelled civilian areas in a guerrilla-held mountain ridge on Thursday.
Israel has said it would complain that guerrillas fired on its forces from inside three villages in the area.

According to witnesses, some 50 shells slammed into the villages of Ain Bouswar and Jba'a on the Iqlim al-Toufah ridge -- which is controlled by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas -- during Thursday's exchange of fire. A civilian woman in Jba'a was hurt by flying debris caused by an exploding shell.

The committee was formed under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April against Hizbollah after exchanges of fire that targetted civilian areas on both sides.

The ceasefire agreement bars the targetting or launching of attacks from civilian areas by both sides. Some 200 Lebanese, mostly civilians, were killed in the April onslaught, dubbed by Israel "Operation Grapes of Wrath".
